Miami aspires to be recognized as an international art hub, with the Pérez Art Museum Miami (PAMM) playing a significant role in this transformation. The museum, donated $40 million by billionaire real estate developer Jorge Pérez, is one of the few major institutions in the United States with a Hispanic name.

Notably, Pérez contributed half of the donation from his personal art collection, aiming to elevate Miami's status on the global art scene. The museum showcases 110 works from Pérez's private collection, housed within a three-story, 200,000-square-foot building designed by Pritzker Prize-winning Swiss architects Herzog & de Meuron.

The museum focuses on international art of the 20th and 21st centuries and is currently showcasing Chinese artist-activist Ai Weiwei's According to What? collection. PAMM is one of the main attractions in Museum Park, which will also house the Patricia and Phillip Frost Museum of Science.

While the naming of the museum after Pérez stirred some controversy, 43 out of 47 board members voted in favor of the change. Some argued that the name should represent Miami's central art museum; however, others viewed it as a symbol of pride for the Hispanic community. Jorge Pérez is the first major donor from the Hispanic community to contribute to an American art museum without causing controversy.

Title Announcement for AMC's "The Walking Dead" Companion Series

Here's some exciting news! The new series, serving as a prequel to the original "The Walking Dead," has been named "Fear The Walking Dead."

During its development season, this spin-off was referred to by code names like Cobalt and Fear The Walking Dead before being officially greenlit for production. AMC made the announcement on March 9th, albeit for a series still unnamed at that time.

Robert Kirkman, creator of "The Walking Dead" comic series, co-wrote the pilot episode alongside Dave Erickson from "Sons of Anarchy." Both Kirkman and Erickson will serve as executive producers, along with Gale Anne Hurd and Dave Alpert from the original series. Erickson will be in charge as showrunner, while Adam Davidson will direct the pilot. Greg Nicotero, responsible for visual effects in "The Walking Dead," will also join the team as an executive producer.

Although AMC has been vague about the plot details, sources suggest that the drama unfolds in Los Angeles at the onset of a zombie outbreak. Although they've confirmed the series takes place in LA, further information is limited to the fact that it explores new characters and storylines.

The cast includes Cliff Curtis known for "Gang Related," who plays Sean Cabrera, a teacher with joint custody of his son. Kim Dickens from "Sons of Anarchy" will co-star as Nancy, a guidance counselor dating Sean. Frank Dillane, famous for "Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince," portrays Nick, Nancy's troubled son dealing with drug issues. Alycia Debnam Carey, starred in "Into the Woods," plays Ashley, Nancy's ambitious daughter eager to leave Los Angeles behind when disaster strikes.

"Fear The Walking Dead" is set to premiere during late summer, with season two scheduled for 2016 (an exact date hasn't been disclosed yet). Meanwhile, the fifth season finale of the flagship series airs on Sunday at 9 p.m. Happy New Year! It looks like it's going to be an interesting year ahead!

Miami, renowned for its tropical climate, retiree community, and Cuban-American population, is making strides towards becoming an international art hub. The catalyst for this change is billionaire real estate developer Jorge Pérez, who donated $40 million, half of which came from his private art collection, to the Pérez Art Museum Miami (PAMM).

Ancient villages have been discovered in Miami, and downtown Miami is undergoing a major revitalization. David Beckham plans to construct a stadium there for his newly announced Miami soccer team. The international art and fashion extravaganza Art Basel, held annually in Miami Beach for over a decade, is the country's leading art fair, attracting tens of thousands of people to the five-day event.

Jorge Pérez hopes that his museum will help propel Miami into the global art scene. Cultural institutions have played a significant role in the city's growth, with this museum being a prime example, according to Pérez, who was interviewed by CNN. Prior to becoming known as the Condo King of South Florida, he started as an urban planner, focusing on low-income housing developments. He later co-founded The Related Group of Florida and worked in high-end condo construction during the 1980s.

In 2005, TIME magazine named him one of the top 25 most influential Hispanics in the United States. He has been featured on Forbes' list of the 400 richest Americans several times, making him the only Latino immigrant to achieve this distinction. Born in Argentina to Cuban parents, Pérez grew up in Colombia before migrating to Miami as a teenager. His lifelong passion for Latin American art can be traced back to his upbringing.

In his early 20s, he began collecting paintings by Roberto Matta, Diego Rivera, Wifredo Lam, and Joaquin Torres-Garcia. Now, 110 works from Pérez's private collection are on display inside the three-story, 200,000-square-foot museum designed by Pritzker Prize-winning Swiss architects Herzog & de Meuron. The $220 million building is distinguished by its tall glass windows, said to be the largest hurricane impact resistant in the world, and 70 self-watering hydroponic gardens designed by French landscape artist Patrick Blanc, which hang from every side of the museum.

PAMM focuses on international art of the 20th and 21st centuries and is currently exhibiting Chinese artist-activist Ai Weiwei's According to What? collection. The museum is located in Museum Park, formerly known as Bicentennial Park, which will also house the Patricia and Phillip Frost Museum of Science, set to open in 2015.

Initially, there was controversy surrounding the naming of the Pérez Art Museum after its benefactor, with four board members resigning in protest. While the majority voted in favor of the renaming, they argued that the name should represent the city's central art museum. Despite the initial strife, Pérez expressed pride at being recognized by the board and said he is honored to have his name associated with a worthy cause. Some argue that Miami takes its art more seriously than science when it comes to naming rights, but the name change has been well-received by the community. So far, the Pérez Art Museum has reached the 90% mark in its $220 million capital campaign.

The exciting news is out! The companion series to the hit show The Walking Dead has been given a title - Fear the Walking Dead. This series will serve as a prequel to the original and has been through development stages under the codenames Cobalt and Fear the Walking Dead.

AMC announced the series pickup and renewal for the yet-to-be-titled spin-off on March 9th. The show's executive producer, Robert Kirkman (who also created the comic book series of The Walking Dead), co-wrote the pilot with Dave Erickson from Sons of Anarchy. Erickson will serve as showrunner, and Adam Davidson has been appointed to direct the pilot. Greg Nicotero, responsible for the visual effects of The Walking Dead, will also be involved in this series as an executive producer.

Although AMC remains tight-lipped about the specifics of Fear the Walking Dead's plot, sources suggest that the drama unfolds in Los Angeles at the start of the zombie outbreak. AMC has confirmed that it is set in Los Angeles but has revealed little beyond stating that it will focus on new characters and storylines.

Cliff Curtis (Gang Related) stars as Sean Cabrera, a teacher with a shared son with his ex-wife. Kim Dickens from Sons of Anarchy is set to co-star as Nancy, a guidance counselor who works at the school with Sean and is romantically involved with him. Frank Dillane (Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince) portrays Nancy's son Nick, who has struggled with drug problems. Alycia Debnam Carey (Into the Woods) plays Nancy's ambitious daughter Ashley, who dreams of leaving Los Angeles for Berkeley when the apocalypse occurs.

Fear the Walking Dead will premiere in late summer, with a second season set for 2016. The official premiere date has yet to be announced. The season five finale of the flagship series airs Sunday at 9 p.m.

Miami is renowned for its tropical climate, retiree community, and Cuban-American population, but not as a significant international art hub. However, this could change with the efforts of billionaire real estate developer Jorge Pérez.

Pérez, who is also an art enthusiast, donated $40 million to the Pérez Art Museum Miami (PAMM), making it one of the few major institutions in the United States with a Hispanic name. This museum has played a critical role in Miami's growth, according to Pérez himself.

Before becoming known as the Condo King of South Florida, Pérez started his career as an urban planner, focusing on low-income housing developments. He then co-founded The Related Group of Florida and worked in high-end condo construction in the 1980s. In 2005, TIME magazine named him one of the top 25 most influential Hispanics in the United States. Pérez has also appeared on Forbes' list of 400 richest Americans several times, making him the only Latino immigrant to do so.

Born in Argentina to Cuban parents, Pérez grew up in Colombia before moving to Miami as a teenager. His lifelong passion for Latin American art stems from his upbringing. In his early 20s, he began collecting paintings by Roberto Matta, Diego Rivera, Wifredo Lam, and Joaquin Torres-Garcia. Today, 110 works selected by the museum from Pérez's private collection are on display at PAMM, housed in a three-story, 200,000-square-foot building designed by Swiss architects Herzog & de Meuron.

The museum focuses on international art of the 20th and 21st centuries. Currently, it is exhibiting Chinese artist-activist Ai Weiwei's According to What? collection. PAMM is one of the main attractions in Museum Park, which will also house the Patricia and Phillip Frost Museum of Science, set to open in 2015.

The Pérez Art Museum had a bit of controversy surrounding its naming, with some board members resigning in protest when it was decided to name the museum after Pérez. However, Pérez has been involved with the museum since before the building project began and said he is honored by the recognition.
